title: Customer Advocacy Roadmap Statement of Needs & Commitment Allocator
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Create a repeatable "statement of needs" intake and commitment allocator for top accounts and escalations so PMs and ENG can translate high-touch asks into a bounded roadmap commitment with clear SLAs and scope fallback. Background: We get frequent escalations from top customers asking for roadmap priority or SLA-level changes. Current intake is ad-hoc (email/zoom → Slack → engineering triage) and causes inconsistent promises and misaligned expectations across Sales, CSM, and Eng. This initiative intends to: 1) formalize a short intake artifact (Statement of Needs) that captures impact signals, urgency, and acceptable fallback; 2) provide a lightweight scoring model that outputs an initial commitment tier and suggested delivery window; 3) embed the allocator into PM triage workflows and Console intake dashboards so commitments are visible and auditable. Scope: - Define minimal (1-page) Statement of Needs template (problem, business impact, required outcome, acceptable alternatives, deadline). - Build a scoring model weighted by ARR, contractual SLA, legal/regulatory requirement, strategic partnership status, and operational risk. - Implement a small Console view for intake reviewers (PMs) that shows score breakdown, suggested commitment tier, and recommended fallback policy (defer/partial/alternative). - Author commitment contract language for CSM/Sales to use when confirming acceptance with the customer. Out of scope (initial): full workflow automation (Slack bot) and billing/contract amendments. Constraints and trade-offs: - Accuracy vs speed: the scoring model must be conservative to avoid overcommitting; we will bias toward partial scope + runway reservation rather than full-scope guaranteed delivery. - Visibility vs noise: do not surface every intake to execs—only those crossing the high-score threshold. - Legal involvement: commitments that change contractual SLAs require Legal review; the intake must escalate such cases automatically. Success metrics (initial): - Time from intake to PM decision <= 3 business days. - Percentage of top-account escalations with a Statement of Needs artifact >= 90% within 60 days of rollout. - Reduced unplanned sprint churn from escalations by 35% in the first two cycles. Implementation phases: Phase 1 (MVP) - Template + scoring prototype + reviewer cheat sheet + pilot with 3 top accounts. Phase 2 - Console integration + audit trail + Sales/CSM templates. Phase 3 - Automation + contract amendment flows. Decision points: - Scoring weights (revenue vs legal/regulatory vs strategic) need PM/Revenue/Legal signoff. - Commitment tiers (Immediate SLA change, Fastpass Sprint, Deferred Runway Reservation) to be finalized in the PM sync.
